Marathon Petroleum fell 3% today after climbing sharply over the previous three trading days, retreating to levels last seen a week ago. The stock's pullback follows news that Russian crude production has rebounded significantly—reaching 8.73 million barrels per day in October—pushing global oil markets back into surplus (more supply than demand). When the world has excess oil, refiners like Marathon face margin pressure because they can't command premium prices for the fuel they produce.

The broader refining environment offers some offset: U.S. refineries are running at 95.2% capacity, and heating oil prices remain elevated at 59% above last winter's levels, which supports margins on those products. However, the recent jump in transportation costs and cautious retailer inventory behavior signal softer demand ahead, which could weigh on fuel consumption as we head into the winter season.
